terms.grammar: adjective, mostly plural; no masculine nominative singular
evidence: Sen. Ep. 15.10: quid tibi cum cēterīs?
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: cēterī are the others besides those named, of the same kind; reliquī, those left over (see the rest).

terms.gloss: the others that remain, the remaining
terms.comment: Those left when some have been taken out: reliquīs septem (diēbus), on the other seven days.

evidence: Gell. 19.5.10: aliī indūtiās cum eā variē factitābant
terms.comment: Others, some others; for “some … others”, see some.

phrases.latin: hōc certāmine puer quīdam audentior cēterīs in ulteriōra tendēbat
phrases.english: in this contest one boy, bolder than the others, kept swimming further out

phrases.latin: quid tibi cum cēterīs? tē ipse antecessistī
phrases.english: what are the others to you? you have outrun yourself

phrases.latin: nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs cēterīsque, quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat
phrases.english: not for himself alone, but for his wife, his children and the others whom he holds dear and ought to protect

phrases.latin: sacrum Sōlī id animal et ōre ac distīnctū pinnārum ā cēterīs avibus dīversum
phrases.english: the bird is sacred to the Sun, and differs from all the others in its beak and the markings of its feathers

phrases.latin: annum ita dīvīsērunt, ut nōnīs modo diēbus urbānās rēs ūsurpārent, reliquīs septem ut rūra colerent
phrases.english: they divided the year so that they saw to town business only on every ninth day, and farmed on the other seven

phrases.latin: atque ita posteā ego bellum et odium nivī indīxī, aliī indūtiās cum eā variē factitābant
phrases.english: and so from then on I declared war and hatred on snow; others made truces with it now and then

sources: Lewis & Short: ceterus · Lewis & Short: reliquus · Lewis & Short: alius
